text.title: Go Error Handling (AppError + Centralised Mapper) Core Rules
text.summary: 13 testable rules every Go Error Handling (AppError + Centralised Mapper) application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Project MUST define one `apperror.AppError` struct {Code, Message, HTTPStatus, Cause, Stack}; never multiple. It MUST implement both `Error() string` and `Unwrap() error`.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal Go review patterns. Without `Unwrap()`, `errors.As` cannot traverse the chain and every type check breaks at the first wrap. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Errors crossing layers MUST be wrapped with `fmt.Errorf("verb: %w", err)` to preserve the chain. At the HTTP boundary classify with `errors.As` / `errors.Is` — a type assertion `err.(*AppError)` is FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go 1.13 error wrapping. `%v` stringifies and drops the chain; a type assertion matches only the outermost type and silently misses every wrapped error. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Each `internal/<feature>` package MUST expose sentinel vars (`ErrNotFound`, `ErrConflict`).
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go style guide. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Storage-layer sentinels (`sql.ErrNoRows`, `pgx.ErrNoRows`, `redis.Nil`, driver uniqueness violations) MUST be translated to domain sentinels at the repository boundary. A driver error MUST NEVER reach a handler.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal reviews. Driver-specific types create implicit coupling at the wrong layer — the handler cannot know which driver sits below it, so the coupling only surfaces when the driver is swapped. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Errors MUST be logged exactly once — at the outermost handler — not at every layer.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Field guides. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: ONE middleware MUST render `AppError` to the RFC 7807 envelope; handlers return errors, never write JSON.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Hexagonal architecture. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: `fmt.Errorf("...%s", err)` is FORBIDDEN — always `%w` to preserve chain.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go vet checks. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Handlers are declared as a `Handler` type that RETURNS an error (`func(w, r) error`) and are adapted by a single `Wrap` function. A handler MUST NOT write the error response inline.
rule.rationale: An inline response write duplicates the translation logic at every call site, and duplicated translation always drifts. Returning the error puts the mapping in one adapter that a reviewer can read in full.

rule.statement: Panic-recovery middleware MUST be registered BEFORE the error-mapping middleware. Canonical order: RequestID, Recovery, Logger, ErrorMapper, Auth.
rule.rationale: Recovery has to convert the panic into an error before anything can map it. If mapping runs first, a panic bypasses it entirely and the client gets a blank 500 with no body and no code. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.
`http.ResponseWriter` flushes the status on the first body byte; a status set after the body has started is silently discarded and the client sees 200 for a 500.

rule.statement: `golangci-lint` MUST enable `errorlint`, `wrapcheck`, `errcheck` and `nilnil`. The default config is not sufficient.
rule.rationale: Defaults catch neither `%v` wrapping nor unwrapped returns. This explicit set is how the rules above become enforceable rather than aspirational; block the merge on any finding from it.

rule.statement: NEVER export a package-level mutable `*AppError` var. Expose constructor functions (`NewNotFound`, `NewBadRequest`, `NewConflict`, `NewInternal`) that return a fresh instance; immutable sentinels declared with `errors.New` are the only exported error values.
rule.rationale: `ErrNotFound.Message = "X"` mutates a global — one request corrupts state for every subsequent request. It passes in isolation and flakes under load. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: When wrapping at a higher layer, `Wrap` MUST `errors.As` the input and preserve the inner `*AppError`'s `HTTPStatus` and `Code` when one is present. A 404 MUST NOT become a 500 on rewrap.
rule.rationale: Status demotion on rewrap reports client errors as server errors: it corrupts SLO accounting and pages on-call for a 404. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold and no duplicate exists.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.

rule.statement: Update the existing artefact in place (bump version, refresh last_reviewed).
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when a duplicate is found.
